data:
Learn how the SlapRF software and hardware fit together, then install the SlapRF Timing Application on your phone or computer.
Architecture & Modes Understand Software vs. Hardware, Bluetooth Mode vs. USB Mode, and multi-gate splits. Installation Install SlapRF on Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, or Raspberry Pi.
SlapRF separates race logic on your phone or laptop from raw 5.8 GHz signal measurement at the gates, giving you low-cost hardware on the course and full race analytics at the pilot bench.
data.bluetooth-usb-and-poe-network-modes#Blue:
A SlapRF track uses one Hub timer (H1) and up to 6 optional Spoke timers (T1 through T6). All three Hub transport modes support single-gate lap timing and multi-gate section split timing.
Bluetooth ModeUSB ModePoE Network Mode Bluetooth Mode (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) removes all cables between the track and the pilot bench.
Power the Bluetooth Hub (H1) from a LiPo battery (via a 5 V USB-C BEC) or USB power bank and place it directly at the Start / Finish gate. Your phone or laptop stays with you at the bench and connects over Bluetooth Low Energy. Optional Spoke timers (T1 to T5) at split gates link to the Hub over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW, and the Hub forwards every gate reading over Bluetooth.
USB Mode (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) connects the Hub directly to your laptop or Android phone over a USB-C data cable for minimum transport latency.
The host USB port powers H1 directly with no battery required at the bench. Battery-powered Spoke timers (T1 to T6) sit at the track gates, including Start / Finish. If your USB cable reaches the Start / Finish gate, you can also place H1 directly on the Start / Finish gate in your practice session or race Track tab.
PoE Network Mode (slaprf-p4-poe-bridge.bin + slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) runs both power and 100 Mbps Ethernet up to 100 m over a single Cat5e or Cat6 cable to the Start / Finish gate.
Plug a USB Hub (H1) into the USB-A port of a Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH board at the Start / Finish gate and feed it from an 802.3af PoE switch or injector at the pilot bench. Neither board at the gate needs a battery, and optional Spoke timers (T1 to T6) link to H1 over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW. See PoE Ethernet Bridge for the bill of materials and setup steps.
data.mode-comparison#Mode Comparison: Aspect Bluetooth Hub USB Hub PoE Bridge + USB Hub Firmware Image slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin slaprf-xiao-c5.bin slaprf-p4-poe-bridge.bin + slaprf-xiao-c5.bin Host Connection Wireless Bluetooth LE USB-C data cable 100 Mbps PoE Ethernet (TCP/UDP :5480) Hub Power Source LiPo + 5 V BEC (or power bank) Host phone or laptop USB port 802.3af PoE switch or injector Typical Placement At the Start / Finish gate At the pilot bench (or Start / Finish via cable) Up to 100 m away at the Start / Finish gate Wireless Spokes Up to 5 Spokes + Hub (6 gates) Up to 6 Spokes Up to 6 Spokes Transport Latency Low (ideal for solo & club practice) Lowest (< 0.2 ms USB) Sub-millisecond (< 0.5 ms wired LAN) Tip For everyday practice, Bluetooth Mode is the fastest field setup: place one battery-powered Hub at the Start / Finish gate, connect from your phone at the bench, and fly. For formal race heats where lowest wired latency matters most, use a USB Hub or a PoE Bridge.
data.system-overview#System Overview:
Gate timers (H1 and T1 through T6) sweep up to 8 active 5.8 GHz VTX frequencies and stream timestamped RSSI samples to the host device. The SlapRF app filters the live signal stream, detects gate crossings, computes lap and section split times (S1, S2, S3), announces spoken callouts, and stores all session history in slaprf.db.

data:
Download the latest native SlapRF release from GitHub Releases . Each build is self-contained and requires no external runtime or database server.
Note The online preview at https://slaprf.app runs a simulated track for exploring the interface. Because web browsers throttle background tabs and audio, install the native Android app, sideloaded iOS/iPadOS app, or desktop binary below to time real flights.
data.cli-flags#CLI Flags: Flag Default Description -addr 127.0.0.1:8090 HTTP listen address and port. -lan false Bind to 0.0.0.0:8090 for Wi-Fi LAN access (implies -no-browser). -db slaprf.db Path to the database file storing pilots, sessions, and races. -no-browser false Do not launch a browser window automatically on startup. -no-auth false Clear HTTP Basic Authentication credentials on startup. -version false Print the build version and exit.
data.platform-setup#Platform Setup:
AndroidiOS / iPadOSWindowsmacOSLinuxRaspberry Pi Android Open GitHub Releases on your phone or tablet and download slaprf-android-arm64.apk. Tap the downloaded .apk file to install it, allowing installation from your browser or file manager if prompted. Open SlapRF. The app runs the Go timing engine locally on your device with offline storage, spoken callouts, Bluetooth LE, and USB OTG serial support. Tip You can flash XIAO ESP32-C5 boards directly from your Android phone or tablet using the built-in Flasher screen in the SlapRF app over a USB-C data cable.
iOS and iPadOS (Free Sideload) SlapRF ships slaprf-ios-arm64.ipa for iPhones and iPads running iOS or iPadOS 16.0 and newer. You can install it with a free Apple ID (no paid developer account required).
Option A: Sideloadly (Recommended for Windows and macOS) Install Sideloadly on your Windows PC or Mac, then connect your iPhone or iPad over USB once and tap Trust This Computer. Download slaprf-ios-arm64.ipa from GitHub Releases (or click Install via Sideloadly in Settings -> Datasource on https://slaprf.app), enter your Apple ID in Sideloadly, and click Start. On your iPhone or iPad, enable Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Developer Mode, then open Settings -> General -> VPN & Device Management, select your Apple ID profile, and tap Trust. Keep Sideloadly running in the background on your computer with Wi-Fi auto-refresh enabled so the 7-day free signature renews automatically over your home Wi-Fi without plugging in a cable. Option B: SideStore or AltStore (On-Device Updates) Add the SlapRF source URL in SideStore or AltStore for 1-tap installations and updates:
https://slaprf.app/altstore-source.json Supported Hardware on iPhone and iPad SlapRF Bluetooth Hub (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin): Open Network, select SlapRF (Bluetooth), tap Connect, and allow Bluetooth access when prompted. SlapRF PoE Ethernet Bridge (:5480): Connect your iPhone or iPad to the same Wi-Fi LAN (or plug in a USB-C Ethernet adapter), select SlapRF (Network), and tap Connect. Direct USB-C Serial: iOS omits generic CDC-ACM serial drivers, so direct USB Hub links and USB firmware flashing are hidden in the iOS app. Flash boards once from Chrome, Edge, Opera, or Android before pairing on iOS. Windows Download slaprf-windows-amd64.exe from GitHub Releases . Move the executable into a dedicated folder, clear the download flag, and launch it in PowerShell (or move and double-click it in File Explorer): New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$HOME\SlapRF" | Out-Null Move-Item -Force "$HOME\Downloads\slaprf-windows-amd64.exe" "$HOME\SlapRF\slaprf.exe" Unblock-File "$HOME\SlapRF\slaprf.exe" Set-Location "$HOME\SlapRF" .\slaprf.exe SlapRF creates slaprf.db in that folder, starts on http://127.0.0.1:8090, and opens your default browser automatically. macOS Download slaprf-macos-arm64 (Apple Silicon) or slaprf-macos-amd64 (Intel) from GitHub Releases . Move the binary into a dedicated folder, clear the macOS quarantine attribute, and run it: mkdir -p ~/SlapRF && mv ~/Downloads/slaprf-macos-* ~/SlapRF/slaprf cd ~/SlapRF xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./slaprf 2>/dev/null || true chmod +x ./slaprf ./slaprf SlapRF starts on http://127.0.0.1:8090 and opens your browser. When connecting to a SlapRF Bluetooth Hub for the first time, allow Bluetooth access for your terminal application if macOS prompts you. Use Chrome, Edge, or Opera when flashing firmware over USB in Flasher. Linux (x86_64 Desktop) Download slaprf-linux-amd64 from GitHub Releases . Move the binary into a dedicated folder, mark it executable, and run it: mkdir -p ~/SlapRF && mv ~/Downloads/slaprf-linux-amd64 ~/SlapRF/slaprf cd ~/SlapRF chmod +x ./slaprf ./slaprf SlapRF starts on http://127.0.0.1:8090 and opens your default browser. For USB Serial timers (/dev/ttyACM*), add your user to dialout (Ubuntu/Debian) or uucp (Arch) and log out and back in once: sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER To grant immediate access on XIAO ESP32-C5 (303a:1001) without logging out, add a udev rule ordered before 73-seat-late.rules: echo 'SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ENV{ID_VENDOR_ID}=="303a", ENV{ID_MODEL_ID}=="1001", MODE="0660", GROUP="dialout", TAG+="uaccess"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/70-slaprf-esp32c5.rules sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=tty For Bluetooth Hub (slaprf_ble) mode, SlapRF powers on BlueZ automatically and selects the first active adapter. If your PC has multiple Bluetooth controllers (such as motherboard Bluetooth plus a USB dongle), set SLAPRF_BLE_ADAPTER=hci1 to pick a specific adapter. Raspberry Pi (ARM64) Note Hardware testing is verified on Raspberry Pi 4 Model B running Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit). Use a 64-bit (aarch64) OS image; 32-bit (armhf) Raspberry Pi OS is not supported.
Connect the Raspberry Pi to 5 GHz Wi-Fi or wired Ethernet, then download slaprf-linux-arm64 from GitHub Releases onto the Pi: mkdir -p ~/SlapRF && cd ~/SlapRF curl -fLO https://github.com/kaack/SlapRF/releases/latest/download/slaprf-linux-arm64 chmod +x ./slaprf-linux-arm64 ./slaprf-linux-arm64 On a headless SSH or systemd session (no desktop display), SlapRF automatically enables LAN mode (0.0.0.0:8090) and prints its browser URL (such as http://raspberrypi.local:8090). For USB Hub (slaprf) mode, Raspberry Pi OS includes your user in the dialout group by default, so /dev/ttyACM0 works immediately with no extra rules. Important Raspberry Pi 4 + Bluetooth Hub (slaprf_ble) Requirements:
Do not enable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi on the Pi. The Raspberry Pi 4 shares one CYW43455 radio and PCB antenna between 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE. Connect the Pi via 5 GHz Wi-Fi or Ethernet (or connect the Hub over USB-C with slaprf-xiao-c5.bin if only 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is available). Keep 30 cm to 1 m (1 to 3 ft) between the Pi and the Hub. Placing the Hub antenna right beside the unshielded Raspberry Pi board saturates its 2.4 GHz receiver and prevents Bluetooth connections. Power the Pi from a dedicated 5 V / 3 A USB-C supply. Do not power the Pi and XIAO timers from the same USB hub.
data.verified-platforms#Verified Platforms: Platform / Device Bluetooth Hub USB-C Hub USB Flasher LAN Timers Verified Environment & Notes Android (ARM64 Phone / Tablet) Verified on Android (arm64-v8a APK); use a USB-C OTG data cable for USB Hub and in-app Flasher. iOS / iPadOS (ARM64 iPhone / iPad) Free sideload (slaprf-ios-arm64.ipa on iOS/iPadOS 16.0+ via Sideloadly or SideStore); verified in iOS Simulator, pending physical iPhone/iPad test. Windows 11 (x86_64) Verified on Windows 11 (slaprf-windows-amd64.exe, WinRT Bluetooth LE and COM serial). macOS (Apple Silicon) Verified on Apple Silicon (slaprf-macos-arm64, CoreBluetooth and /dev/cu.usbmodem*); Intel (amd64) binary also built in CI. Linux Desktop (x86_64) Verified on Ubuntu x86_64 (slaprf-linux-amd64, BlueZ and /dev/ttyACM*). Raspberry Pi 4 (ARM64) Verified on Raspberry Pi 4 Model B (Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit); requires 5 GHz Wi-Fi or Ethernet for Bluetooth Hub. Verified on physical hardware Built (pending physical hardware test) Not supported
data.wi-fi-lan-sharing#Wi-Fi LAN Sharing:
By default, the desktop binary binds to 127.0.0.1:8090 for local use on that machine. To host SlapRF on a trackside laptop or headless Raspberry Pi so pilots and spectators can view live standings over Wi-Fi, pass -lan:
WindowsmacOS / Linux .\slaprf.exe -lan ./slaprf -lan SlapRF listens on 0.0.0.0:8090 and prints its local network URL (such as http://192.168.1.42:8090). Open Settings -> Authentication in the UI to set an HTTP Basic Auth username and password so spectators cannot modify race settings. If you get locked out, start the binary once with -no-auth to clear saved credentials.

data:
Build and flash DIY 5.8 GHz gate timers using off-the-shelf Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 boards with zero soldering.
Parts & Assembly Bill of materials, battery power, U.FL antenna setup, and gate placement. Flashing Firmware Flash Bluetooth Hub, USB Hub, Spoke, and PoE Bridge firmware from the app or browser. Status LED Patterns Live animations and millisecond timing strips for every yellow LED blink state. PoE Ethernet Bridge Power and connect a USB Hub up to 100 m away over a single 802.3af PoE Ethernet cable.

Configure and flash Hub (H1) and Spoke (T1 through T6) firmware onto Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 boards, or flash the optional PoE Ethernet Bridge (slaprf-p4-poe-bridge.bin) onto a Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH, directly from your desktop browser below or from the built-in Flasher screen inside the SlapRF Android and desktop apps over USB-C. No ESP-IDF toolchain, Python install, or serial driver is needed.
data.before-flashing#Before Flashing: Requirement Details Supported Host Built-in Flasher in the SlapRF Android or desktop app (over USB-C / OTG), or desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera for the browser flasher above. USB-C Data Cable Plug directly into your phone or computer port (avoid charge-only cables and unpowered hubs). Matching Versions When updating SlapRF firmware, re-flash both the Hub (H1) and all Spokes (T1-T6) so their ESP-NOW protocol matches.
data.browser-flasher#Browser Flasher:
Connect your XIAO ESP32-C5 with a USB-C data cable in Chrome, Edge, or Opera to flash directly from this page, or flash from the Flasher screen inside the SlapRF Android or desktop app:
Open Firmware Flasher Warning Connect only one XIAO ESP32-C5 board at a time while flashing. During 2.4 GHz radio calibration bursts, each ESP32-C5 draws up to 320 mA, and plugging multiple boards into shared USB ports can cause 5 V sag and interrupted writes.
data.flash-via-usb#Flash via USB: Click Flash to USB, select the USB serial port in the browser chooser, and click Connect. Erasing, writing, and verification finish in about 20 seconds without holding the BOOT button.
data.led-quick-reference#LED Quick Reference:
After flashing, the onboard yellow LED (GPIO27) indicates board status. See Status LED Patterns for live animations and millisecond timing charts.
Board State Blink Pattern Meaning Hub Ready Single 70 ms blip every 2.0 s USB Hub active, or Bluetooth Hub connected to your paired host. Spoke Synced Double 70 ms blip every 2.0 s Spoke (T1-T6) paired with the Hub over ESP-NOW and sweeping. BLE Pairing Mode Fast double-blink every 1.0 s Unclaimed Bluetooth Hub ready to pair with a phone or laptop. Searching / Waiting Steady 1 Hz (500 ms ON / 500 ms OFF) Spoke searching for Hub, or paired BLE Hub waiting to reconnect. Identify 3 quick flashes + pause (600 ms cycle) Identify mode triggered from the SlapRF UI. Radio Fault Continuous 10 Hz strobe (50 ms ON / 50 ms OFF) 5.8 GHz radio check failed; power-cycle or re-flash the board.
data.open-flasher#Open Flasher: Click Open Firmware Flasher above to launch the firmware wizard.
data.select-device-and-role#Select Device and:
In Step 1 (What are you flashing?), pick Gate Timer (XIAO ESP32-C5) or PoE Bridge (Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH; see PoE Ethernet Bridge).
PoE Bridge: Advances straight to Flash bridge in Step 2. Gate Timer: Pick Hub (H1, one per course) or Spoke (wireless split gates) in Step 2, then choose Bluetooth (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) or USB cable (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) for a Hub, or timer label T1 through T6 for a Spoke in Step 3.

data: Each battery-powered SlapRF Gate Timer snaps together from off-the-shelf parts with no soldering or custom PCBs required, and fits inside a compact 3D-printed case for field durability.
data.attach-antenna#Attach Antenna:
Align the included dual-band (2.4 / 5 GHz) U.FL antenna plug flat over the gold receptacle on the XIAO ESP32-C5 and press straight down until it clicks into place.
Warning Always snap on the U.FL antenna before applying power. Operating without the antenna severely reduces both 5.8 GHz VTX sensitivity and 2.4 GHz wireless range.
data.bill-of-materials#Bill of Materials:
One Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 draws under 100 mA at 5 V (0.5 W), so a compact 650 mAh 3S LiPo pack runs a gate timer for roughly 8 hours.

Short USB-C PD Cable $5.00 - $9.00 3S-6S LiPo Pack Powers the gate timer in the field (any spare XT60 flight pack or low-current USB power bank works). Tattu 850mAh 3S $15.00
data.board-layout#Board Layout: Use this callout diagram to locate the USB-C port, yellow status LED (L), U.FL antenna connector, BOOT button (B), and RESET button (R) on the XIAO ESP32-C5:
data.connect-power#Connect Power: Plug a 3S-6S LiPo battery into the XT60-to-USB-C adapter, then connect the short USB-C cable to the XIAO ESP32-C5. Set the timer flat on the ground centered inside the gate opening.
data.example-track-costs#Example Track Costs: Setup Boards Needed Typical Total 1-Gate Bluetooth 1 Bluetooth Hub (H1) + spare LiPo $23 - $35 3-Gate Bluetooth 1 Bluetooth Hub + 2 Spokes (T1, T2) $69 - $105 3-Gate Wired USB 1 USB Hub (laptop-powered) + 3 Spokes (T1-T3) $76 - $112
data.flash-firmware#Flash Firmware: Connect one XIAO ESP32-C5 at a time over USB-C to your phone (in the SlapRF Android app) or computer and flash its role using the in-app Flasher or the Flashing Firmware page. Mark each board (H1, T1, T2, T3) with tape or a paint pen so placement at the field takes seconds.
data.hardware-assembly#Hardware Assembly:
The setup below shows the barebones way to put a gate timer together using a USB-C adapter and a spare LiPo pack. While barebones wiring works right away for testing, we recommend buying or 3D printing an enclosure (see Recommended Cases below) to protect the XIAO board and U.FL antenna from prop strikes, dust, and wet grass on the course.

data.recommended-cases#Recommended Cases:
Enclosing each timer keeps the snap-on U.FL antenna strain-relieved and shields the electronics at the base of the gate. If you do not own a 3D printer, local print shops or online print services can print these STL/3MF files in PETG, ASA, or TPU for a few dollars:
Enclosure Design Highlights Model Link Compact XIAO Case Minimal snap-fit case with a USB-C cutout and dedicated internal space for the included Seeed U.FL antenna. Pair with your external USB-C adapter and LiPo pack. MakerWorld #3567817 Biscuit 18650 Tube All-in-one rugged tube enclosure that houses the XIAO ESP32-C5, internal antenna, and an integrated 18650 battery compartment in a single unit. MakerWorld #2612343 More XIAO C5 Cases Community enclosures, mounts, and gate clips designed for the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 form factor. Browse MakerWorld
data.track-placement#Track Placement:
Center each gate timer on the ground at the base of its gate with the flat antenna element facing upward toward the flight path. Keep pilot pits and powered VTX benches at least 5 to 10 meters away from active gates so parked quads do not hold channel RSSI elevated.
On tight technical courses where an adjacent lane passes right beside a gate, placing the XIAO inside a shallow open-top metal cup or foil-lined tray shields side-lobe RF energy so only direct overhead passes register a peak.

data: Place Hub H1 directly at the Start / Finish gate up to 100 m (328 ft) away using a single Ethernet cable for both power and data. A Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH board powers H1 over USB-A with no battery needed at the gate, while optional Spoke timers (T1 through T6) link wirelessly to H1 as usual.
data.bill-of-materials#Bill of Materials:
The PoE Bridge and Hub H1 draw under 2 W combined, so any standard 802.3af PoE switch or inline PoE injector powers the gate continuously all day.
Part Purpose Example Source Est. Cost ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH Bridges Hub H1 on USB-A to 100 Mbps Ethernet with integrated onboard 802.3af PoE power (SKU 32832 Basic Kit). Waveshare Amazon Board Docs $24.99 - $30.00 XIAO ESP32-C5 Hub H1 timer at the Start / Finish gate (flashed with the standard USB Hub image; includes snap-on U.FL antenna). Short USB-A to USB-C $5.00 - $8.00 802.3af PoE Switch or Injector Supplies power and network connectivity from the pilot bench over one Ethernet cable. PoE Switch PoE Injector $15.00 - $28.00 Cat5e or Cat6 Cable Runs power and 100 Mbps Ethernet between the pilot bench and the Start / Finish gate (up to 100 m). Outdoor Cat6 Cable $10.00 - $25.00
data.connect-at-the-gate#Connect at the Gate: Unplug the USB-C programming cable from your computer. Plug Hub H1 into the USB-A port on the Waveshare board with a short USB-A to USB-C data cable, then plug your PoE Ethernet cable into the RJ45 port. Both boards power on automatically from the Ethernet cable.
data.connect-in-slaprf#Connect in SlapRF:
Connect your laptop or phone to the same network (wired Ethernet or Wi-Fi router connected to your PoE switch, or a direct cable from your laptop to a PoE injector) and open Network in the SlapRF desktop or Android app:
Set Timing system to SlapRF (Network). Click Discover, select the detected PoE Bridge, and click Connect. Confirm Hub H1 appears as Active with live RSSI bars. Tip Connecting to a bridge in SlapRF (Network) adds a PoE Bridge tab to the main navigation so you can inspect Ethernet link speed, switch between DHCP and a static IPv4 address, change USB-A baud rate, restart the attached USB timer, or reboot the bridge remotely with no serial commands.
data.flash-the-poe-bridge#Flash the PoE Bridg:
Plug the USB-C port on your Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH into your computer using a USB-C data cable. Click Open PoE Bridge Flasher below, click Flash PoE Bridge to USB, and select the USB Single Serial port:
Open PoE Bridge Flasher If you have not flashed your XIAO ESP32-C5 Hub (H1) yet, flash it with the Hub (USB cable) option on Flashing Firmware.

data:
Every Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 board drives its onboard yellow user LED (GPIO27) from an independent 10 ms hardware timer in the SlapRF firmware, keeping blink timing exact regardless of channel sweep load.
Each card below pairs a real-time yellow LED simulation on the left with a millisecond square-wave timing strip underneath.
data.diagnostics--faults#Diagnostics \u0026 F: LIVE Identify Timer (Find My Gate) All Boards 3 quick 50 ms flashes followed by a 350 ms pause Triggered when you click Identify on a timer in the SlapRF UI to locate which physical board corresponds to H1, T1, or T2. The 350 ms pause between 3-flash groups distinguishes it from the continuous 10 Hz fault strobe. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 3 x (50 ms ON · 50 ms OFF) + 300 ms extra dark pause (600 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Live Spectrum / Debug Stream Active (5 Hz) All Boards Steady 5 Hz fast blink Indicates an active diagnostic LIVE or wideband 5.8 GHz spectrum SCAN LIVE stream over the serial or BLE console. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 100 ms ON · 100 ms OFF (200 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE 5.8 GHz Radio Self-Check Fault (10 Hz) All Boards Continuous 10 Hz rapid strobe (no pause) The ESP32-C5 5.8 GHz radio path failed its boot or runtime health check (!rf_ok). Unplug power for 5 seconds, verify stable 5 V supply voltage, and re-flash the latest SlapRF firmware if the strobe continues. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 50 ms ON · 50 ms OFF continuous (100 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF
data.normal-operation#Normal Operation: LIVE Hub Ready & Active USB Hub · Connected Bluetooth Hub Single 70 ms blip every 2.0 seconds The Hub (H1) passed its 5.8 GHz radio self-check and is ready for timing. On a USB Hub, this pattern starts immediately after boot. On a Bluetooth Hub, it appears once your paired phone or laptop connects and authenticates over Bluetooth LE. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 70 ms ON · 1930 ms OFF (2000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Spoke Joined & Synced Spoke (T1 to T6) Double 70 ms blip every 2.0 seconds The wireless Spoke locked onto the Hub’s 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW beacon within the last 2.5 s, synchronized its clock, and is streaming 5.8 GHz RSSI sweeps to the Hub. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 70 ms ON · 150 ms OFF · 70 ms ON · 1710 ms OFF (2000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF
data.pairing--search#Pairing \u0026 Search: LIVE Bluetooth Hub: Pairing Mode (Unclaimed) Bluetooth Hub Fast double-blink every 1.0 second The Bluetooth Hub has no saved host bond yet and is open for Claim-on-Pair. Open Network in the SlapRF app and connect; the first device to connect claims the Hub so nearby spectators cannot take over your timer at the field. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 80 ms ON · 100 ms OFF · 80 ms ON · 740 ms OFF (1000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Waiting for Link (1 Hz Slow Blink) Spoke Searching · Paired Bluetooth Hub Disconnected Steady 1 Hz blink (50% duty cycle) On a Spoke (T1-T6), the board is searching for a Hub over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW. On a claimed Bluetooth Hub (H1), the board is advertising over Bluetooth LE and waiting for its paired phone or laptop to reconnect. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 500 ms ON · 500 ms OFF (1000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Clear Bluetooth Pairing (Hold BOOT for 3.0 s) Bluetooth Hub Solid ON while holding BOOT -> 800 ms rapid burst -> Pairing Mode To pair a claimed Bluetooth Hub with a different phone or laptop, hold the BOOT button (GPIO28) while powered. The yellow LED stays solid ON while held, flashes a rapid 800 ms burst at 3.0 s when the saved host key is cleared, and enters Pairing Mode. TIMING STRIP (4.8 s WINDOW) Hold BOOT 3.0 s (Solid ON) -> 60 ms ON / 60 ms OFF burst (800 ms) -> Pairing Mode 0 ms 1200 ms 2400 ms 3600 ms 4800 ms ON OFF

data:
Step-by-step guides for the five most common ways pilots and race directors use SlapRF.
Solo & Club Practice Set up pilots, connect your timer, and fly with AI detection or calibrated DSP thresholds. Multi-Gate Section Splits Add wireless Spoke timers around the course to measure S1, S2, and S3 split times. AI Detection & Training Fly with the pre-trained SlapRF Base model, train custom models, or switch to DSP thresholds. Running a Race Event Build brackets, run heats with automated horns, review waveforms, and sync MultiGP. RotorHazard & LapRF 8-Way Run the SlapRF Timing Application with existing RotorHazard or LapRF hardware.

SlapRF supports two gate crossing detection modes for Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 timers: an on-device AI neural detector and a traditional DSP (Enter and Exit dBm threshold) detector. You can switch between both modes at any time from the Track tab in Practice or Races.
data.ai-vs-dsp-detection#AI vs. DSP Detection: Mode How It Works Best For AI (SlapRF Base or Custom Model) Evaluates the 5.8 GHz RSSI pass shape over time with a 1D convolutional neural network (1D-TCN). Needs no dBm threshold setup. Flying immediately at 25 mW to 200 mW+, multi-gate tracks with varying gate distances, and dipole multipath notches. DSP (Enter and Exit Thresholds) Opens a crossing window when RSSI rises above Enter dBm, tracks the peak, and closes the pass when RSSI drops below Exit dBm. Deterministic dBm cutoff control, bench walk-tests, and setups where you want manual per-gate Enter and Exit lines.
data.compare-accuracy-and-activate#Compare Ac: When training finishes (typically under 90 seconds on laptop or phone), inspect the DSP vs. AI scorecard (Passes found, False triggers, and Accuracy). Select your new model in the Track -> Crossing detector menu to fly with it in Practice or Races.
data.fine-tune-or-train-in-ai-training#Fine-T:
Open the AI Training tab inside your Practice session:
Fine-Tune an Existing Model (Recommended): Select SlapRF Base (or any trained model) in the models list. Check Include other practices if you want to combine multiple sessions, then click Fine-Tune. SlapRF leaves the original model untouched, saves a new copy named SlapRF Base FT (followed by SlapRF Base FT (1), SlapRF Base FT (2), and so on for additional runs), and selects the new copy automatically. Add a Named Model (Train from Scratch or Fine-Tune): Type a model name in Search or add model… and click + Add. Set Base model to Empty (train from scratch) and click Train, or choose any trained model in Base model and click Fine-Tune to adapt it into your new named model.
data.fly-out-of-the-box-with-slaprf-base#Fly:
SlapRF ships with a built-in model named SlapRF Base (1P), pre-trained on verified 5.8 GHz multi-gate hardware telemetry. You do not need to calibrate dBm thresholds before flying.
Open your session’s Track tab in Practice or Races. In the Crossing detector card, select AI. Confirm SlapRF Base (1P) is selected in the model menu. Under Timing rules, set Beep on crossing to On (or Off). In AI mode, the app plays a confirmation beep each time the model confirms a gate pass. Tip 2L Tune (Optional) · Leave 2L Tune off for standard flights with SlapRF Base or a custom trained model. Enable 2L Tune only if you want the detector head to adapt on the fly after your first two laps on an unfamiliar gate layout.
data.record-a-practice-session#Record a Pract: Connect your timers, start a Practice session, and fly one or more battery packs at normal pace. Pause the session when finished.
data.review-and-clean-up-crossings#Review and:
Open the Review tab inside your Practice session and click RSSI on Lap 1 to open the single-lap waveform editor:
Use Prev and Next in the chart toolbar to step through each lap. If you swapped batteries mid-session without pausing, click Break in the modal header during the idle gap so battery-swap dead air is excluded from laps and training data. To fix any missed or extra pass, unlock the chart (Lock icon), click + to place a missing gate pass at its RSSI crest, drag existing markers onto the true peak, or click × on false triggers. On desktop builds, you can also click Auto-Label to label gate passes in track order automatically.
data.share-models-and-datasets-across-devices: At the bottom of the AI Training tab, use Export Bundle and Import Bundle to transfer a portable .tar.gz archive containing your labeled practice sessions, .rfbin waveforms, and trained custom models between your phone and desktop computer.
data.switch-to-traditional-dsp-thresholds#Swi:
If you prefer traditional threshold detection with explicit Enter and Exit dBm lines, switch the detector to DSP:
Open the Track tab in Practice or Races and select DSP in the Crossing detector card. Start your session, open Signals, and fly 2 to 3 passes through each gate at race speed. Select a timer chip (H1 or T1-T6) and tap Calibrate to compute Enter and Exit dBm thresholds from your recorded peaks and noise floor. To adjust thresholds manually, open Fine-tune on any selected timer in Signals: Enter Threshold (dBm): Raise this value (closer to 0 dBm) if adjacent lanes cause false triggers. Lower it if fast or wide passes are missed. Exit Threshold (dBm): Keep this value 6 dB to 12 dB below Enter so dipole signal dips do not split one pass into two crossings. Beep on crossing: Choose Off, Enter, Peak, or Exit.
data.train-or-fine-tune-a-custom-ai-model#Tra:
While SlapRF Base works out of the box, you can fine-tune SlapRF Base or train a dedicated model on your own sessions to match a specific VTX power level, antenna polarization, indoor venue, or tight gate spacing.
SlapRF records raw .rfbin RSSI waveforms automatically during every Practice session.

data: Connect the SlapRF App to existing RotorHazard or ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way hardware over LAN or USB without building new timers.
data.choose-your-mode#Choose Your Mode:
Open Network in the native SlapRF desktop or Android app and select your hardware from the Timing system dropdown:
Dropdown Option Connection Hardware & When to Choose It LapRF 8-Way (Network) Ethernet LAN (TCP :5403) ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way puck plugged into a field router or network switch. LapRF 8-Way (USB) USB CDC serial (115200 baud) ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way puck plugged directly into your phone or computer over USB (no router or IP setup). RotorHazard (Network) Wi-Fi or Ethernet (HTTP / Socket.IO :5000) Complete RotorHazard server (Raspberry Pi + RX5808 shield) on the local network. RotorHazard (USB) USB serial (115200 or 921600 baud, API 36) Standalone RotorHazard RX5808 node board (ESP32-C5, STM32, Arduino, or RP2040) plugged directly into USB with no Raspberry Pi. Note While a timer is connected (or connecting), the Timing system dropdown on Network locks to prevent accidental mode switches mid-session. Click Disconnect next to the dropdown to unlock it and switch to a different timing system.
data.laprf-8-way-emulator#LapRF 8-Way Emulato: When timing with SlapRF DIY hardware or RotorHazard on Windows, macOS, Linux, or Android, open Settings -> LapRF 8-Way emulator to host a local ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way TCP :5403 server. External LapRF-compatible race software (such as LiveTime) and broadcast overlays can connect to port 5403 to receive live crossings from SlapRF in real time. (The emulator hides automatically while LapRF 8-Way (Network) or LapRF 8-Way (USB) is active so port 5403 never loops back into itself.)
data.laprf-8-way-setup#LapRF 8-Way Setup:
LapRF 8-Way (Network)LapRF 8-Way (USB) LapRF 8-Way (Network) Use LapRF 8-Way (Network) when your LapRF 8-Way puck connects to the same Wi-Fi router or Ethernet switch as your laptop, Raspberry Pi, or phone.
Open Network and select LapRF 8-Way (Network) in Timing system. Click Connect next to the dropdown to discover powered-on pucks on TCP :5403, or enter the IP address (default 192.168.1.2) and port (5403) manually. Confirm the timer card shows supply voltage, Synced clock offset, and live 300-3500 RSSI bars across the 8 receiver slots. SlapRF pushes pilot frequencies and thresholds automatically when a session or heat starts. LapRF 8-Way (USB) Use LapRF 8-Way (USB) when plugging a LapRF 8-Way puck directly into your laptop, Raspberry Pi, or Android phone over USB (115200 baud CDC serial). Note that the LapRF 8-Way still requires external 10 V-25 V DC pack power on its XT60 input to power its 5.8 GHz RF receivers.
Power the LapRF 8-Way from a LiPo battery via XT60 and connect its USB port to your host device. Open Network and select LapRF 8-Way (USB) in Timing system. Click Connect USB next to the dropdown and select the LapRF serial port. Confirm the timer card reports supply voltage, Synced clock offset, and live 8-slot RSSI readings.
data.multi-unit-courses--section-splits#Multi: Most clubs place one 8-channel RotorHazard or LapRF 8-Way timer at the Start / Finish gate. If you connect two or more RotorHazard or LapRF timers at once, open your Practice session or Race workspace, select the Track tab, and drag each unit onto the track line in flight order to record S1, S2, and S3 section splits. For cable-free split gates across a field without running LAN cables or Raspberry Pis to each gate, use battery-powered SlapRF DIY Timers.
data.rotorhazard-setup#RotorHazard Setup:
RotorHazard (Network)RotorHazard (USB) RotorHazard (Network) Use RotorHazard (Network) when your RotorHazard timer runs a Raspberry Pi host on Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Open Network and select RotorHazard (Network) in Timing system. Click Connect next to the dropdown to scan the LAN for RotorHazard servers on port 5000, or enter the server IP and port manually (for example, 192.168.1.101 and 5000). When prompted by the sign-in dialog, enter the RotorHazard admin username and password (default admin / rotorhazard) and click Sign in & Connect. Verify the device card reports Admin, live 0-255 node RSSI bars, and clock sync. Assign pilot VTX channels in Pilots (or in a Race heat) and fly Practice or Races. RotorHazard (USB) Use RotorHazard (USB) when plugging a standalone RotorHazard serial node board (binary serial API 36, 1 to 8 RX5808 seats) directly into your computer or Android phone over USB-C.
Plug the RotorHazard node board into your host with a USB data cable. Open Network and select RotorHazard (USB) in Timing system. Click Connect USB next to the dropdown, leave Baud Rate on Auto (115200 / 921600) (or select 115200 / 921600), and select the serial port. Confirm the device card reports Connected, node count, serial RTT, and live 0-255 RSSI bars. You can also run 5180-5945 MHz spectrum sweeps and waterfall plots on Debug.

data: A single gate measures total lap time, while adding wireless Spoke timers (T1 through T6) around the course breaks every lap into section splits (S1, S2, S3) so you can see exactly where time is gained or lost.
data.flash-spokes#Flash Spokes: Use the Firmware Flasher (or the built-in Flasher in the SlapRF Android or desktop app over USB-C) to assign each Spoke board a unique slot (T1 through T6) on the same firmware version as H1.
data.fly-or-calibrate-gates-in-dsp-mode#Fly (:
Tap Start in your Practice session:
In AI mode (SlapRF Base): Fly immediately through all gates with no per-gate dBm calibration (see AI Crossing Detection & Training). In DSP mode: Fly 2 to 3 complete laps through every gate, open Signals, select each gate timer (or use each timer row on mobile), and tap Calibrate to compute Enter and Exit thresholds.
data.how-splits-work#How Splits Work:
When timers sit at sequential gates along the flight path, SlapRF measures each interval independently before closing the full lap at Start / Finish:
Track Segment Recorded Split Start / Finish -> Gate 2 Section 1 (S1) Gate 2 -> Gate 3 Section 2 (S2) Last Gate -> Start / Finish Final section + completed lap time Every Spoke streams its 5.8 GHz RSSI sweeps to H1 over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW while H1 continuously aligns each Spoke’s clock.
data.place-timers#Place Timers: In Bluetooth Hub mode, place H1 at Start / Finish and place Spokes (T1, T2, …) at split gates around the track. In USB Hub mode, keep H1 plugged into your laptop or phone at the bench, place T1 at Start / Finish, and place T2, T3, … at split gates. Raising a bench Hub onto a table or crate off damp grass improves long-range 2.4 GHz reception.
data.reading-split-data#Reading Split Data:
After flying a pack, open the Laps and Trends tabs in Practice to review performance across the track:
View What It Shows Lap Table Side-by-side S1, S2, S3 splits for every lap alongside your Theoretical Best Lap (sum of your fastest individual splits). Section Consistency Per-section variance charts highlighting which obstacle or turn costs the most time across a pack. Per-Gate Fine-Tune Select an individual timer chip (such as T2) in Signals to adjust one tight or high-speed gate without changing the rest of the course.
data.set-gate-order#Set Gate Order: Open Network to confirm H1 and all powered Spokes report Online. Open Practice (or Races), select your session or event, and open its Track tab. Drag your active timers onto the track line in flight order and click the checkered flag under your Start / Finish gate. Each session and race saves its own gate order and timing rules independently.

data: Set up a single-gate practice session, fly immediately with the pre-trained SlapRF Base AI detector (or calibrated DSP thresholds), and hear spoken lap callouts.
data.add-pilots#Add Pilots: Open Pilots and enter each pilot’s callsign, optional phonetic spelling for text-to-speech pronunciation, and default 5.8 GHz channel (such as R1 5658 or F4 5800).
data.audio-callouts#Audio Callouts: Enable Beep on crossing in your session’s Track tab (Off | On in AI mode, or Off | Enter | Peak | Exit in DSP mode) for an immediate confirmation tone when a gate pass registers. Open Settings -> Announcer to choose your offline voice, volume, and whether spoken callouts read pilot name plus lap time or lap time alone.
data.configure-session-track--crossing-detect:
Open Practice, select or create a practice session, and open its Track tab:
Confirm your active gate timer (H1 or T1) sits on the track line with the checkered Start / Finish flag selected. Choose AI or DSP in the Crossing detector card. AI uses the pre-trained SlapRF Base (1P) model with no dBm threshold setup. DSP uses traditional Enter and Exit dBm hysteresis thresholds. Adjust track-wide or per-timer Timing rules (Min lap time, Max lap time, Min crossing time, and Beep on crossing) if needed. Each practice session stores its own track layout and timing rules independently.
data.dsp-threshold-tuning#DSP Threshold Tunin:
If you select DSP in Track -> Crossing detector, most setups need no manual adjustment after tapping Calibrate. To adjust a specific gate manually, select its timer chip in Signals and open Fine-tune:
Parameter Adjustment Guide Enter Threshold (dBm) Signal level that starts a crossing. Raise it (closer to 0 dBm) if nearby lanes trigger false laps; lower it if fast passes are missed. Exit Threshold (dBm) Signal level that closes the crossing window (6 to 12 dBm below Enter prevents double-triggers). Min Lap Time (s) Minimum seconds between consecutive valid laps for the same pilot. Any timer with custom threshold or timing overrides displays a sky-blue indicator in Signals and Track. Tap Clear calibration on that timer at any time to restore default values.
data.fly-and-calibrate-if-using-dsp#Fly (and:
Open Pilots in your Practice session to assign active pilot channels, tap Start, and fly:
In AI mode: Arm your quad and fly through the Start / Finish gate. SlapRF Base detects gate crossings immediately with no threshold calibration. You can later fine-tune or train custom models in Review and AI Training (see AI Crossing Detection & Training). In DSP mode: Switch to Signals, fly 2 to 3 passes through the Start / Finish gate at race speed, select your gate timer, and tap Calibrate. SlapRF inspects your recorded peaks and noise floor and sets the Enter and Exit dBm levels automatically.
data.prerequisites#Prerequisites: Install the SlapRF Timing Application on your Android phone or laptop and prepare one flashed Hub timer (H1, either Bluetooth or USB).
data.select--connect-hub#Select \u0026 Connec:
Open Network and choose your mode in the Timing system dropdown:
SlapRF (Bluetooth): Power H1 (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) at the Start / Finish gate, click Pair Device (or Connect for a previously paired Hub), and select your Hub. SlapRF (USB): Plug H1 (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) into your phone or computer over USB-C (with T1 powered at Start / Finish, or H1 placed directly at the gate) and click Connect USB. Confirm the connected timer chip shows a green live indicator.

data: SlapRF includes a full race control workspace for club races, qualifiers, elimination brackets, and MultiGP chapter events.
data.create-or-import#Create or Import:
Open Races from the main navigation to start a new event:
Option Workflow Built-in Templates Start from Qualifying + Finals, Double Elimination, Single Elimination, Open Qualifier, Points Mains, Chase the Ace, or a Blank Custom Format. MultiGP Import Add your chapter API key in Settings -> MultiGP to pull registered pilots, VTX channels, and event rounds directly from MultiGP.
data.format--heats#Format \u0026 Heats:
Inside an event workspace, open Setup to configure stages, advancement rules, and heat lineups using either editor:
Format Canvas: Drag stage nodes and connect advancement wires visually (for example, routing Top 8 from Qualifying to Championship Double Elimination and 9th-16th to Consolation). Setup Table: Edit heat counts, pilot slots, VTX channels, heat duration, and scoring format (Fastest 3 Consecutive, Single Fastest Lap, Total Laps + Time, Points, or Chase the Ace). Tip Enable Simulator mode before race day to test custom stage progressions, advancement rules, and heat tie-breakers end to end without hardware.
data.live-race-control#Live Race Control:
Switch to the Race tab when pilots step up to the flight line:
Select the upcoming heat and confirm pilot VTX channel assignments. Click Start Heat. SlapRF plays the staging callout, runs the configured start delay, sounds the start horn, and arms crossing detection. During the heat, live standings, split deltas, and spoken lead/lap announcements update in real time. When the clock expires, the finish horn sounds while timing stays open until active pilots finish their current lap. Click Next Heat to advance; when a stage completes, downstream brackets seed automatically.
data.marshal-review#Marshal Review: When a pilot challenges a missed crossing or an early launch, open the completed heat’s review panel in Race Control to inspect the recorded Start / Finish RSSI waveform alongside every crossing marker. Race directors can invalidate a false pass, insert a missed crossing at its exact waveform peak, or schedule a re-run, with standings updating immediately.
data.results--multigp#Results \u0026 MultiGP: Open the podium view at any time to inspect overall event standings. For MultiGP chapter races, click Upload to MultiGP to publish completed round times and final placements back to your MultiGP event page.
data.track--timing-rules#Track \u0026 Timing:
Inside an event workspace, open Track to configure the course for that specific race:
Drag active timers (H1, T1-T6, RotorHazard, or LapRF units) onto the track line in flight order and click the checkered flag under the Start / Finish gate. For SlapRF timers, select AI (SlapRF Base or a custom trained model) or DSP (Enter and Exit thresholds) in Crossing detector (see AI Crossing Detection & Training). Set track-wide Timing rules (Min lap time, Max lap time, Min crossing time, and Beep on crossing), or select an individual timer chip to override rules for a single gate. Each race stores its own track and timing rules independently from practice sessions and other races. When a race is completed or scrapped, its recorded track and timing rules lock read-only.

data:
Screen-by-screen UI documentation, OpenAPI / AsyncAPI server specifications, and hardware troubleshooting solutions.
App & UI Reference Guide to every SlapRF screen and the 3-tier timing rules. API Reference OpenAPI 3.1 REST spec and AsyncAPI 3.0 WebSocket stream for overlays and integrations. Troubleshooting Solutions for flashing, Bluetooth, Spoke pairing, and gate detection.

SlapRF Portable and the SlapRF Android LAN host expose a versioned HTTP REST API (/v1/...) and real-time WebSocket streams (/v1/ws/...) on port 8090 for building custom OBS stream overlays, LED gate controllers, race scoreboards, and automation scripts.
data.50-hz-binary-telemetry-frame-layout#50 H:
Each binary WebSocket message begins with a 4-byte little-endian header followed by count packed frame records (20 + 4 * rssiCount bytes per record; 52 bytes per record when rssiCount == 8):
Byte Offset Type (Little-Endian) Field Description 0 uint8 version Wire format version (always 1). 1 uint8 rssiCount Number of RSSI channel floats per record (typically 8). 2..3 uint16 count Number of packed telemetry records in this batch. 4 + i*stride + 0 uint8 timerId Physical timer ID (1 = Hub H1, 2..7 = Spokes T1..T6). 4 + i*stride + 1 uint8 reserved Always 0. 4 + i*stride + 2..3 uint16 batteryMv Timer supply voltage in millivolts (for example, 4120). 4 + i*stride + 4..7 uint32 seqNum Monotonic sweep sequence counter from the timer. 4 + i*stride + 8..15 float64 timestampUs Microsecond timestamp in server timebase. 4 + i*stride + 16..19 float32 noiseFloorDbm Estimated 5.8 GHz noise floor in dBm (for example, -94.5). 4 + i*stride + 20.. float32[rssiCount] rssi Per-slot smoothed RSSI values in dBm.
data.javascript--typescript-websocket-client-: const ws = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8090/v1/ws/stream"); ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer"; ws.addEventListener("message", (event) => { if (typeof event.data === "string") { const msg = JSON.parse(event.data); if (msg.type === "lap") { const { lap } = msg.payload; console.log(`[LAP] ${lap.callsign} Lap ${lap.lapNumber}: ${lap.lapTimeSec.toFixed(3)}s`); } else if (msg.type === "crossing") { const c = msg.payload; console.log(`[GATE] ${c.callsign} -> ${c.gateName} (${c.peakRssiDbm.toFixed(1)} dBm)`); } return; } // Decode 50 Hz binary RSSI telemetry batch const view = new DataView(event.data); if (view.byteLength < 4 || view.getUint8(0) !== 1) return; const rssiCount = view.getUint8(1); const count = view.getUint16(2, true); const stride = 20 + 4 * rssiCount; for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) { const base = 4 + i * stride; const timerId = view.getUint8(base); const batteryMv = view.getUint16(base + 2, true); const seqNum = view.getUint32(base + 4, true); const timestampUs = view.getFloat64(base + 8, true); const noiseFloorDbm = view.getFloat32(base + 16, true); const rssi = []; for (let ch = 0; ch < rssiCount; ch++) { rssi.push(view.getFloat32(base + 20 + ch * 4, true)); } // Use { timerId, batteryMv, seqNum, timestampUs, noiseFloorDbm, rssi } } });
data.quick-start-rest-examples#Quick-Start RE:
Fetch active state and print pilot callsigns and best laps:
curl -s http://localhost:8090/v1/state | jq '.summaries[] | {callsign, totalLaps, bestLapSec}' Create a new pilot (201 Created + Location header):
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8090/v1/pilots \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"callsign":"VORTEX","phoneticName":"vor-teks"}' Start the currently staged heat in the active race session:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8090/v1/race/sessions/current/heats/current:control \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"action":"start","preemptOngoing":true}'
data.rest-api-openapi-310#REST API (OpenAPI 3:
Resource-oriented /v1/* endpoints across system state, pilots, hardware timers, practice sessions (including per-session tracks and timing rules), race sessions (including per-race tracks and timing rules), hardware links, simulator controls, and storage.
Interactive Reference: Browse REST API Docs OpenAPI Specification: Download openapi.yaml
data.server-base-url--authentication#Server B:
By default, SlapRF Portable binds to http://127.0.0.1:8090. To allow external devices on the same Wi-Fi or Ethernet LAN (such as an OBS streaming PC or field scoreboard) to access the /v1 REST and WebSocket endpoints, start SlapRF with -lan:
./slaprf -lan -addr 0.0.0.0:8090 If Basic Auth is enabled under Settings -> Authentication, pass a standard Authorization: Basic header on REST requests (or create an authenticated session check via POST /v1/auth/sessions).
data.stream-api-asyncapi-300#Stream API (Asyn:
Real-time WebSocket streams (/v1/ws/*) delivering JSON event envelopes (crossing, lap, filtered, race, practice, config) and 50 Hz binary RSSI telemetry batches.
Interactive Reference: Browse Stream API Docs AsyncAPI Specification: Download asyncapi.yaml
data.websocket-binary-telemetry-wire-format-v: While all JSON event envelopes (crossing, lap, filtered, race, practice, config, usbStatus) are documented interactively in the WebSocket API (AsyncAPI 3.0) reference page, /v1/ws/stream also multiplexes high-rate 5.8 GHz RSSI telemetry batches at 50 Hz (20 ms) as compact little-endian WebSocket Binary Frames (application/octet-stream).

Quick diagnostics and fixes for USB flashing, wireless connectivity, power supplies, and gate detection.
data.android-app-does-not-open#Android App Do:
If the Android app closes immediately or fails to open from the launcher:
If the SlapRF Startup Diagnostic screen appears, tap Share Log or Save File… to save slaprf-startup-log.txt. If no screen appears, tap the SlapRF app icon one more time so SlapRF exports the previous failed launch trace to Downloads/slaprf-startup-log.txt. Open the Android Files app, select Downloads, and locate slaprf-startup-log.txt (this file records the Android build, startup checkpoints, native exit reason, and slaprf.log tail with no personal race data). Open a bug report on GitHub Issues and attach slaprf-startup-log.txt.
data.false-adjacent-laps#False Adjacent Laps:
If flying on a nearby lane triggers laps on an adjacent gate:
Fly 2 to 3 clean passes through the gate and click Calibrate, or open Fine-tune and raise the Enter threshold closer to 0 dBm (for example, -58 dBm to -50 dBm). Set Min Lap Time just below your fastest realistic lap on the course. On tight tracks, set the XIAO inside a shallow open-top metal cup or foil-lined tray under the gate to block side-lobe RF from neighboring lanes.
data.hub-not-found#Hub Not Found:
If your phone or laptop does not discover the Bluetooth Hub in Network:
Verify the board was flashed with the Bluetooth Hub image (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) and shows either the fast double-blink (Pairing Mode) or 1 Hz slow blink. Open Network and confirm the Timing system dropdown is set to SlapRF (Bluetooth) (if another timer is active, click Disconnect first to unlock the dropdown). Disconnect any other phone or browser tab already linked to the Hub (BLE advertising pauses while an active host is connected). To switch the Hub to a new phone, computer, or Raspberry Pi, click Forget Device in Network while connected on the old device, or hold BOOT on the Hub for 3.0 s until the rapid LED burst clears the previous bond. On Linux, SlapRF powers on the default BlueZ adapter automatically. If your host has more than one Bluetooth controller, run bluetoothctl list and set SLAPRF_BLE_ADAPTER=hci1 (or your active adapter name) if needed.
data.in-app-operational-logs#In-App Operation:
SlapRF records user actions, race and practice events, completed laps, and hardware link transitions in a rolling slaprf.log file alongside the app on desktop, Android, and iOS (and in a bounded 1,000-line in-memory buffer in standalone Browser Demo Mode), tagging simulated activity with [SIM]:
Open Settings and scroll to the Diagnostics section at the bottom of the page. Change the log level from INFO (default) to DEBUG or TRACE before reproducing an issue. Click Download to save slaprf-YYYY-MM-DD.log for inspection or bug reports, then switch the level back to INFO (default).
data.interrupted-flash#Interrupted Flash: If flashing halts partway through or boards reset randomly on USB, unplug any extra XIAO boards so only one board is connected at a time. Multiple ESP32-C5 radios calibrating on 2.4 GHz simultaneously can droop a shared laptop 5 V rail.
data.missed-fast-passes#Missed Fast Passes:
If high-speed passes through a gate do not register:
Confirm the pilot’s channel in Pilots matches the exact VTX band and frequency (and that Pit Mode is off). Remove inactive pilot slots from the session so timers sweep fewer frequencies and sample each active pilot faster. Open Fine-tune on that gate timer and lower the Enter threshold slightly (for example, -48 dBm to -55 dBm).
data.poe-bridge-not-discovered#PoE Bridge Not:
If Discover in Network -> SlapRF (Network) does not list your ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH bridge:
Confirm your laptop or phone is on the same local network as the PoE switch or router (or enter the bridge IP address and port 5480 directly and click Connect). Verify the RJ45 link LEDs on the ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH are lit and that Hub H1 is plugged into the USB-A port with a USB data cable (flashed with the USB cable Hub image, not Bluetooth). If needed, re-flash the bridge from PoE Ethernet Bridge.
data.power-bank-shutoff#Power Bank Shutoff: Because a XIAO ESP32-C5 draws under 100 mA, some phone power banks assume nothing is connected and shut off after 30 to 60 seconds. Power gate timers from a 3S-6S LiPo pack with an XT60-to-USB-C 5 V BEC (which never auto-sleeps), or enable trickle-charge mode on your power bank.
data.raspberry-pi-bluetooth-fails-to-connect-:
On Raspberry Pi 4 (CYW43455, and other Raspberry Pi models with a shared wireless chip), 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE share a single onboard 2.4 GHz radio and unshielded PCB antenna. Both 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi traffic and close-range RF overload block Bluetooth Hub (slaprf_ble) connections (le-connection-abort-by-local):
Do not use 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi on the Raspberry Pi. Connect the Pi to 5 GHz Wi-Fi or wired Ethernet and disable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi autoconnect so live browser traffic does not preempt Bluetooth LE packets: # Check active Wi-Fi frequency (~5xxx MHz = 5 GHz, ~24xx MHz = 2.4 GHz) nmcli -f IN-USE,SSID,CHAN,FREQ dev wifi # Disable autoconnect on a 2.4 GHz network profile sudo nmcli connection modify "<2.4GHz-SSID>" connection.autoconnect no If only 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is available at your track, flash the USB Hub image (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) and connect the Hub (H1) to the Raspberry Pi with a USB-C data cable instead of Bluetooth. Move the Hub 30 cm to 1 m (1 to 3 ft) away from the Raspberry Pi. Setting the XIAO ESP32-C5 whip antenna within a few inches of the Raspberry Pi drives 2.4 GHz RSSI above -30 dBm, saturating the Pi’s receiver and dropping GATT handshakes. Use a dedicated 5 V / 3 A USB-C power supply. Do not power both a Raspberry Pi and XIAO ESP32-C5 timers from the same computer USB hub, as 2.4 GHz radio calibration bursts can droop a shared 5 V rail.
data.spoke-stays-offline#Spoke Stays Offline:
If a Spoke (T1-T6) blinks slowly at 1 Hz and stays offline in Network:
Power on the Hub (H1) first and verify it is online. Re-flash the Hub and all Spokes from the same SlapRF release so their ESP-NOW packet versions match. Check that the snap-on U.FL antenna is firmly seated on both boards and that no two Spokes share the same slot ID (T1-T6):
data.usb-port-missing#USB Port Missing:
If the XIAO ESP32-C5 does not appear in the browser serial port chooser:
Swap to a known USB-C data cable (many bundled cables are charge-only with no data wires). Plug directly into your Android phone (using the SlapRF app) or a computer USB port rather than an unpowered hub or dock (use desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera if flashing from a web browser). On Linux, confirm your user is in the dialout or uucp group so /dev/ttyACM0 can be opened. If a board is unresponsive, hold the tiny BOOT button (B, bottom-right of the XIAO) while plugging in USB-C, release BOOT, and click Flash to USB:

data: Reference guide to the screens, live signal scope controls, and crossing detection parameters in the SlapRF Timing Application.
data.app-screens#App Screens: Screen Purpose Practice Practice session directory and workspace (Pilots, Track, Overview, Laps, Trends, Signals, Review, Analytics, and AI Training). Each session stores its own track layout, .rfbin waveform trace, and timing rules. Races Event creation, MultiGP import, per-race Track & timing rules editor, visual Format Canvas brackets, live Marshal / Race Control horns, and Review waveforms. Pilots Pilot directory with callsigns, phonetic TTS spellings, and default 5.8 GHz channels (Raceband, Fatshark, Boscam, IMD6). Network Timing system selector (SlapRF (USB), SlapRF (Bluetooth), SlapRF (Network), LapRF 8-Way (Network), LapRF 8-Way (USB), RotorHazard (Network), RotorHazard (USB)), connection manager, topology graph, and live RSSI monitor. PoE Bridge Shown while connected to a bridge in SlapRF (Network). Displays live Ethernet link speed, IPv4/MAC details, attached USB-A device status, DHCP vs. static IPv4 settings, USB-A baud rate, attached USB device restart, and remote bridge reboot. Flasher Built-in wizard (on Android and desktop) for flashing Hub, Spoke, and ESP32-P4 PoE Bridge firmware, inspecting board configuration, or factory-erasing boards over USB-C. Debug Live 5.8 GHz spectrum and waterfall analyzer, raw USB/Bluetooth timer console, and RF health checks. Simulator Multi-pilot 5.8 GHz physics track simulator for testing track layouts, threshold behavior, and race brackets without hardware. Settings Datasource (Demo vs. SlapRF Server and Simulator toggle), MultiGP API key, Announcer voice & horn levels, LapRF 8-Way emulator, Authentication, .json database backup/restore, and slaprf.log diagnostic log level (ERROR to TRACE), download, and clear controls. On mobile, swipe left or right across the screen to move between Races, Practice, Pilots, Network, and secondary screens, or tap More on the right side of the bottom bar.
data.crossing-detection--rules#Crossing Detec:
Each Practice session and Race Track tab includes a Crossing detector card that switches between AI mode and traditional DSP mode (see AI Crossing Detection & Training):
AI Mode: Evaluates 5.8 GHz RSSI waveforms with the built-in SlapRF Base (1P) neural model or a user-trained custom model from Practice -> AI Training, with an optional 2L Tune adaptive head toggle and Off | On crossing beeps. DSP Mode: Runs a traditional hysteresis detector (Enter dBm -> peak tracking -> Exit dBm) with per-track, per-timer, and per-pilot-at-timer overrides in Track and Signals -> Fine-tune. Parameter Role Detector Mode (AI / DSP) Selects neural waveform pass detection (SlapRF Base or custom model) or traditional Enter / Exit dBm threshold hysteresis. Enter Threshold (dBm, DSP) RSSI level required to open a crossing window in DSP mode. Exit Threshold (dBm, DSP) RSSI level required to close the crossing window and record the peak timestamp in DSP mode (6 to 12 dBm below Enter prevents double-counting). Min Crossing Time (s, DSP) Minimum duration RSSI must remain inside the DSP crossing window, rejecting brief single-sample RF spikes (SHORT). Min Lap Time (s) Minimum valid lap time between consecutive Start / Finish crossings for the same pilot (SHORT). Max Lap Time (s) Maximum duration before a long pause (such as landing to swap batteries) starts a fresh out-lap instead of recording a slow lap (LONG). Beep on Crossing Plays an immediate confirmation tone when a gate crossing registers (Off | On in AI mode; Off | Enter | Peak | Exit in DSP mode).
data.signals-controls#Signals Controls:
Available inside Practice -> Signals and Race -> Signals:
Control Behavior Prev | Live | Next Pause and scrub backward or forward through recorded RSSI history, or return to live streaming. Auto X Switch the horizontal scope span between 1 s, 15 s, 60 s, 5 min, 10 min, or automatic fit. Auto Y Toggle automatic vertical dBm range fitting versus full dBm scale. Timer Chips / Rows Filter by All, H1, or T1-T6 to inspect Enter and Exit lines. Select an individual timer (or use its row actions on mobile) to calibrate or open Fine-tune. Calibrate Appears for a selected timer once flight pass data is recorded. Computes Enter and Exit dBm levels from recent passes, with Clear calibration to restore defaults.
